findings.summary: Comment/behaviour mismatch on the head_seq read path: the block comment states 读失败即响亮失败（非零退出）, but _read_tick_head_seq swallows the child's stderr (2>/dev/null) and returns exit 0 with the sentinel HEAD_SEQ_READ_FAILED. The sentinel is loud enough for §1.3 (it is not a silent N/A and the entry still records it per attempt), so this is non-blocking; but discarding stderr loses the named root cause (missing channel / list-endpoint shape change / token error) that src/e0c2-read-tick-head-seq.ts:36-42 deliberately emits, and the comment should be corrected to match the actual contract.

Carry-over observation from the attempt-2 final review, still applicable: the driver unconditionally puts a {"seed":true} trigger on every invocation, and the entry re-invokes it with the same DD_RUN_ROOT (hence the same TRIGGER_STORE_DIR) each drain. A seed trigger claimed in a later drain takes tick.md's first-round path (no --prev-*), resetting that chain's coverage/zeroGrowthRounds. Convergence is still reachable within a single drain (continuation triggers carry the counters), and the cross-drain loop retries with backoff, so this is not blocking; worth watching the actual convergence round count during 判据 9/11 on the real machine.
